findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Acknowledge in the plan that AC3 reverses CriterionBank's documented run-scoped / 'no cross-run reuse' invariant and address how concurrent closes of the same ticket avoid colliding on the newly-shared keyed bank location.
evidence: completion_banking.py:396-404 CriterionBank docstring: 'Lives under .rebar/workflow_runs/<run_id>/bank/ (run-unique so concurrent closes cannot collide; no cross-run reuse).'
Plan: 'persist the CriterionBank keyed by (ticket, criterion-text hash, HEAD tree hash / --ref tree); a re-verify credits still-valid banked PASS verdicts'
findings.finding: AC3's cross-run CriterionBank persistence contradicts the existing CriterionBank's documented run-scoped invariant ('no cross-run reuse'; run-unique dir chosen 'so concurrent closes cannot collide'), and the plan neither acknowledges overturning it nor addresses the concurrent-close collision hazard that motivated run-scoping.
scenarios: Two concurrent closes of the same ticket now share a keyed bank location instead of run-unique dirs
Reviewer expects the plan to state that the run-scoped invariant is being deliberately changed

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the AC3 edit targets and consumers outside completion.py: completion_banking.py (CriterionBank.for_run keying, BankStamps/resolve_bank_stamps) and completion_recovery.py (CriterionBank.for_run caller).
evidence: completion_recovery.py:464 'bank = _bank.CriterionBank.for_run(ctx.run_id, stamps, repo_root=ctx.repo_root)'
completion_banking.py:322 BankStamps carries ticket_id/material_fingerprint/tree_sha (the seam AC3 would re-key against)
Plan header scopes mechanics to 'completion.py' and never names completion_banking.py / completion_recovery.py
findings.finding: AC3's persistence/keying change lands in src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_banking.py (CriterionBank, BankStamps, resolve_bank_stamps) and its consumer completion_recovery.py (CriterionBank.for_run call), but the plan's mechanics/edit narrative names only completion.py, leaving the actual edit targets and consumer unenumerated.
scenarios: Author estimates blast radius from the plan and misses the recovery orchestrator seam
for_run signature / dir-keying change ripples into completion_recovery.py

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify AC3's cross-run bank as a distinct ticket-scoped store (not the run-scoped CriterionBank): define its key ((ticket, criterion-text hash, tree_sha)), where it lives, when it is written vs. discarded (surviving re-verify but cleared on close-success), and how concurrent closes on the same ticket avoid the collision that today's run-scoping prevents.
evidence: CriterionBank docstring: 'Lives under .rebar/workflow_runs/<run_id>/bank/ (run-unique so concurrent closes cannot collide; no cross-run reuse)'
for_run() keys the dir by run_id; _path() keys files by criterion_id, not by (ticket, criterion-text hash, tree hash)
bank.discard() is called after finalize on BOTH the primary-success path (recovery.py:487) and the recovery path (recovery.py:576), so a subsequent re-verify's new run_id opens a fresh empty bank
The BankStamps preflight/mismatch machinery already carries tree_sha + material_fingerprint — but as a same-run drift guard, not a cross-run cache key
findings.finding: AC3's cross-run criterion-bank persistence structurally contradicts the existing CriterionBank, which is deliberately run-scoped (per-run_id directory, keyed by criterion_id, discard()ed after every finalize) with the stated invariant 'run-unique so concurrent closes cannot collide; no cross-run reuse.' The plan reuses the CriterionBank name but requires a different key ((ticket, criterion-text hash, tree hash)), a survive-across-runs lifecycle, and cross-run reads — without stating how it preserves the concurrent-close collision protection that run-scoping provides. Two concurrent closes on the same ticket would now share the same bank keyspace.
scenarios: A re-verify after exhaustion opens a new run_id, finds an empty bank, and re-proves everything from scratch — AC3's converge-across-runs goal silently fails
Two operators/agents close/re-verify the same ticket concurrently and now write into a shared cross-run keyspace, the exact collision run-scoping prevented
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the run-scoped CriterionBank for in-run banking and add a SEPARATE ticket-scoped 'verdict cache' (e.g. .rebar/completion_cache/<ticket>/<criterion-hash>-<tree_sha>.json) that a re-verify reads to credit still-valid PASS entries; write cache entries only on validated PASS, invalidate on tree/text mismatch via the existing _stamp_mismatch seam, and guard concurrent same-ticket writes (lockfile or atomic write-rename) since the cache is no longer run-unique.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define AC3's invalidation granularity: justify whole-repo HEAD-tree keying (accepting that any unrelated commit invalidates the cache) OR key reuse on a narrower per-criterion signal (evidence-path subtree / material_fingerprint) so unrelated commits do not wipe still-valid banked verdicts.
evidence: _resolve_tree_sha: 'The committed HEAD tree sha of repo_root' via `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` — a whole-repo tree, not a per-criterion evidence subtree
_stamp_mismatch fires when stored.tree_sha != fresh.tree_sha for the entire repo
AC3: 'invalidating entries when the tree or criterion text changed'
findings.finding: AC3 relies on invalidating banked entries 'when the tree or criterion text changed,' but the existing tree stamp is the whole-repo HEAD tree sha (_resolve_tree_sha runs `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`). Under that key, ANY unrelated commit to the repo (a doc typo, an unrelated ticket's change) rotates the tree_sha and invalidates ALL banked criteria for ALL tickets, defeating the cross-run reuse the plan is trying to achieve. The plan does not address this coarse-invalidation granularity.
scenarios: Re-verify a 20-AC epic after one unrelated commit landed elsewhere in the repo — the whole-repo tree_sha changed, every banked verdict invalidates, and the re-verify re-proves all 20 from scratch (the whack-a-mole the plan set out to kill)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile item 3 with the EXISTING run-scoped CriterionBank/BankStamps: state what is reused (tree/material invalidation is already implemented) vs newly built, and justify moving from run-scoped to cross-run persistence against the documented concurrent-close collision rationale.
evidence: completion_banking.py CriterionBank docstring: 'Lives under .rebar/workflow_runs/<run_id>/bank/ (run-unique so concurrent closes cannot collide; no cross-run reuse).'

BankStamps docstring already binds ticket_id + material_fingerprint + resolved tree sha and 'a successor preflight re-resolves all three and fails loud on any mismatch, so a bank can never be reused across a material or tree change' — i.e. the proposed (tree hash / criterion-text) keying + invalidation is largely already implemented.

The plan describes item 3 as if introducing new persistence/keying, but this repackages existing BankStamps invalidation while reversing the run-scoping lifecycle without justifying the concurrency-collision tradeoff the original design chose to avoid.
findings.finding: The cross-run CriterionBank persistence (plan item 3 / AC line 3) does not acknowledge that a CriterionBank already exists and is deliberately run-scoped, nor reason about the design decision it reverses.
findings.location: Plan item 3 (Cross-run criterion-bank persistence) and AC line 3
scenarios: Two concurrent epic closes (or a re-verify overlapping a still-running verify) sharing a persistent bank keyed only by (ticket, criterion-text, tree) could read/write each other's provisional verdicts — the exact collision run-scoping was built to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the existing completion_banking.py CriterionBank + BankStamps in item 3, note that tree_sha/material_fingerprint invalidation already exists, and specify how cross-run reuse preserves the concurrent-close safety property that run-scoping provided (e.g. a locking or read-only-credit discipline), or explain why concurrent closes are no longer a concern.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how a cross-run-credited banked PASS verdict is surfaced to the finalizer (e.g. materialized as a synthetic bounded evidence record in the bank vs. merged post-finalizer) so the finalizer's 'one record per expected criterion' + 'evaluate only those records' rule and the coverage check are satisfied without re-proving credited criteria.
evidence: Plan point 3: 'a re-verify credits still-valid banked PASS verdicts without re-proving ... only spends budget on unproven criteria'

Finalizer prompt: 'You receive an ordered list of the ticket's completion criteria and one bounded evidence report for every criterion. Evaluate only those records.' and 'Include exactly one `criteria` record for every expected criterion'

completion_recovery.py:575 runs `self._finalize(...)` over `bank.all()`; a criterion credited from a prior run but not re-proven this run has no bounded evidence report, so the finalizer's per-criterion coverage rule and 'evaluate only those records' instruction have no defined input for it

ABSENCE: the plan never states whether a credited entry is materialized into the bank as a synthetic PASS evidence record, bypasses the finalizer, or is echoed some other way — the decision rule for credited criteria is not co-located with the finalizer surface that consumes them
findings.finding: Plan point 3 credits banked PASS verdicts without re-proving, but does not specify how a cross-run-credited criterion is presented to the tool-free finalizer, whose prompt requires one per-criterion record derived from a bounded evidence report and instructs 'Evaluate only those records' — the credit-vs-evaluate protocol is not co-located with the finalizer schema that must emit the credited criterion's record.
scenarios: A 15-AC epic exhausts budget on run 1, banks 10 PASS + 5 insufficient; run 2 credits the 10 and must produce a full 15-record verdict — the finalizer has no evidence report for the 10 credited criteria

An executor wires cross-run credit but the finalizer's coverage check (completion_recovery.py 'independently verifies complete criterion coverage') rejects a run whose bank lacks records for credited criteria

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the criterion-bank's storage location, an eviction/retirement path (e.g. drop entries whose tree-hash != current HEAD), and concurrency ownership for simultaneous verifies.
evidence: 'persist the CriterionBank keyed by (ticket, criterion-text hash, HEAD tree tree hash / --ref tree)'
No RETIRE/cleanup path, storage medium, or concurrency handling is described

findings.finding: Cross-run criterion-bank persistence introduces durable shared state with no stated retirement/eviction path, no storage location, and no concurrency ownership; the bank can accumulate (ticket x criterion x tree-hash) entries indefinitely.

findings.finding: The plan bundles three deliverables under one unit: (1) raising budget defaults, (2) an evidence-surface scaling term, and (3) a cross-run CriterionBank persistence layer with tree/text-hash keying and invalidation. Items 1-2 are tightly coupled budget-sizing tweaks, but item 3 is a materially different mechanism — a new persistence surface with its own keying, invalidation semantics, and marker rules — that is independently valuable and releasable (the default raise alone resolves the cited exhaustions). Surfacing as an advisory observation: the persistence layer may be a separable child.
findings.location: Plan step 3 (Cross-run criterion-bank persistence) and AC3
scenarios: If persistence proves complex (storage location, cross-shape durability, invalidation edge cases), it could stall the immediately-valuable default/scaling fix that already resolves the reported exhaustions
